name: Treaty with the Chickasaw, 1805
promises: Article 2: the United States would pay $20,000 for the nation and its debts to traders, $1,000 each to George Colbert and O'Koy, and a life annuity of $100 to Chinubbee Mingo, all in specie.
Article 3: the boundary would be marked with a Chickasaw representative, paid $2 a day by the United States.
Article 4: for three years no settlement would be made or permitted on a described part of the cession.
Article 1: a tract of one mile square below the mouth of Duck River was reserved for the chief O'Koy.
today: No court, Indian Claims Commission or Court of Claims finding about this treaty was located. The Chickasaw Nation's Commission claims (Dockets 267, 268 and 269) concern the Leased District, Choctaw freedmen allotments and a tract left out of a Choctaw cession, not this cession.
